evidence_excerpts: Quantum error correction imposes a heavy overhead cost in number of qubits and number of gates, scaling up using quantum error correction is a more distant goal.
To run algorithms involving thousands of protected qubits we’ll need a number of physical qubits which is in the millions, or more.
text: Scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing depends on quantum error correction, but the physical-qubit overhead makes that era a longer-term objective rather than a near-term NISQ capability.
